## Report

The controller supports both Xinput and Dinput modes.  Dinput mostly works out-of-the-box, but the controller reports the analog shoulder triggers as buttons (only on or off), which is a significant usability issue in many applications.

When switched to Xinput mode, the controller doesn't do anything at all.  It doesn't even turn on (the green light doesn't come on when pressing the "Mode" button).

I found [a CLI tool, `xinput_usb_tool`](https://github.com/meghrathod/xinput-controller/blob/main/tools/xinput_usb_tool.c), that apparently was able to get a different Xinput controller working (apparently macOS would see the gamepad once it was activated, but it wouldn't activate the gamepad on its own).  Running `./xinput-usb-tool listen 100 1133 49693`, my F310 turns on in Xinput mode, and controller events are printed in the terminal, though sadly macOS/SDL3 still didn't detect it as a gamepad on my system.

I then found and tried https://github.com/xsyetopz/OpenJoystickDriver/.  It actually detects and activates the F310 in Xinput mode, and the built-in tester showed the controller buttons/sticks/etc working, though some buttons are mis-mapped, and for some reason, the part that actually exposes the virtual gamepad to applications does not seem to be working on my system (SDL3 saw the virtual gamepad, but inputs weren't being passed to it).

Looking at https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/pull/15183, there seems to be some code using libusb to read data from the controller.  Presumably, to properly support Xinput on this controller (and other similar Xinput controllers not properly supported by Apple), libusb would need to be used to directly turn on the controller and read the inputs.

All testing was on macOS 15.7.3, on Apple Silicon.

With https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/pull/15791 and running `testcontroller` with `SDL_JOYSTICK_MFI=0 SDL_HIDAPI_LIBUSB_WHITELIST=0`, the gamepad works properly.  The up vs down appears to be inverted on both joysticks, but otherwise, all functionality appears to be working as expected, including the center "guide" button.

Here's the mapping string generated by `testcontroller` after using the "Setup Mapping" option to fix the joystick up vs down mapping:
